issue.title: test_post_close_plus_one_badge_marker_search_and_json_agree fails under full parallel lane, live
issue.description: tests/test_bead/test_plus_one_presentation.py::test_post_close_plus_one_badge_marker_search_and_json_agree was flagged as a reproducible flake by tools/selection_health --fail-on-new-flake (reproducible_flake_nodeids) against two disjoint full-lane failure records recorded after the sase-iy flake-baseline cutoff bump (commit 83bb8a6f7, effective-after 2026-08-10T16:50:24Z): one at 2026-08-10T17:27:52Z (head 012e1a88b, changed files src/sase/ace/tui/modals/models_panel_rendering.py + tests/test_models_panel_alias_rendering.py) and one at 2026-08-10T19:18:31Z (head 5f6d8ea64, changed files under src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/prompt_input_bar* and prompt_stack*). Neither change set touches this test's file or the bead plus-one/search code it exercises, and the two failures share no common changed file, so the classifier's two-disjoint-change-set reproducible-flake definition is satisfied. Passes cleanly in isolation (1 passed in 1.60s on the current tree). This is the same fails-under-full-parallel/passes-alone signature as the sase-ct flake class, but the node itself (bead plus-one presentation search/JSON agreement) is unrelated to ACE TUI timing/contention, so it is filed as its own node-specific bead per the sase-ct retirement pattern rather than folded into that umbrella. Root cause not yet investigated.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-ct — same fails-under-full-parallel/passes-in-isolation signature as the sase-ct flake class, discovered while re-verifying the flake-baseline exit criterion during sase-ct's retirement (sase-iy.5). sase-ct is being closed as a retired umbrella; this node-specific bead is filed directly rather than corroborated onto it, per the retirement's routing rule.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction during epic sase-j2 landing: just check-full's flake-baseline gate (just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake) flagged this same node as a reproducible flake again on 2026-08-10, unrelated to sase-j2's TUI panel-isolation/zoom changes (which touch only src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_folding_panels.py, tests/ace/tui/test_agent_panel_collapse_isolation.py, tests/ace/tui/test_agent_panel_isolation_revert.py, tests/test_keymaps_display_help.py, and PNG snapshot goldens).

Independent reproduction during epic sase-j3 landing (2026-08-10, master d4b913bb9): just check-full passed every lint gate, SASE validation, committed-plans validation, and the full pytest cost lane, then failed only at the flake-baseline gate (just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake), which named this node plus tests/ace/tui/test_logs_pane.py::test_logs_tab_g_and_shift_g_scroll_detail_extremes. Queried the durable record store directly: this node has three qualifying full-run failures with pairwise-disjoint change sets - head 012e1a88b (src/sase/ace/tui/modals/models_panel_rendering.py + tests/test_models_panel_alias_rendering.py), head 5f6d8ea64 (sase-j3.2's prompt_stack/prompt_input_bar changes), head e01584098 (sase-j3.3's snippet_name_modal/snippet_targets changes). No changed file is common to all three, and none touches tests/test_bead/ or the bead plus-one/search code under test, so this is not attributable to sase-j3. Phase sase-j3.2 separately recorded that the node passed after rebuilding the local sase_core_rs editable wheel, which is worth checking as a candidate mechanism (stale Rust binding in an ephemeral workspace) alongside the parallel-lane hypothesis.

payload.entry: CONTEXT from epic sase-j8's land agent: landing sase-j8 required bumping the flake-baseline 'effective-after' cutoff in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt from 2026-08-10T16:50:24Z to 2026-08-10T23:36:35Z (one second past commit 9c46891c5), because the gate was judging this epic's own pre-fix history for tests/test_keymaps_registry_loading.py::test_stitches_action_override_wins_over_legacy_commits_alias. payload.entry: Backlog triage (owner-requested seven-bead cut, 2026-08-12): the node is listed under a '# sase-j6' comment in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt at HEAD 62951abcb, so the flake-baseline gate is not red on it. Same fails-under-full-parallel/passes-in-isolation class as sase-jb and sase-jq; sase-jq stays open as the class owner (its nodes are still unbaselined and gate-blocking). Note sase-jj, which stays open, is the separate deterministic cause for this exact node in PyPI-resolved environments (sase-core-rs floor 0.24.0 predates the observed_since search indexing), so fixing the floor may clear this node outright. Reopen with a +1 if it survives that.
